<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[ar:المراتب الاثنتا عشر]][[be:Сістэма дванаццаці рангаў]][[en:Twelve Level Cap and Rank System]][[fa:دوازده سطح کلاه و سیستم رتبه]][[fr:Système des douze niveaux de rang]][[ja:冠位十二階]][[ko:관위십이계]][[nl:Twaalf Hofrangen (Japan)]][[pl:System dwunastu rang]][[ru:Система двенадцати рангов]][[sh:Sistem dvanaest rangova]][[th:ระบบยศผ้าโพกหัวสิบสองชั้น]][[uk:Система дванадцяти рангів]][[zh:冠位十二阶]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[Category:Has wikidata]][[d:Q2448809]] Wikidata name: Twelve Level Cap and Rank System [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 05:32, 12 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|Wikidata entry Wikidata name: [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 10:11, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Short description|Cap and Rank systems established during the Asuka period}} {{nihongo|'''The Twelve Level Cap and Rank System'''|冠位十二階|Kan'i Jūnikai}}, established in 603, was the first of what would be several similar cap and Rank systems established during the [[:en:Asuka period|Asuka period]] of [[:en:Japanese history|Japanese history]].<ref name=samurai>{{cite web |url=http://wiki.samurai-archives.com/index.php?title=Court_Ranks |title=Court Ranks }}</ref> It was adapted from [[Nine-Rank system|similar systems]] that were already in place in [[:en:Sui dynasty|Sui dynasty]] [[:en:China|China]], [[:en:Baekje|Paekche]] and [[:en:Goguryeo|Koguryŏ]]. The officials wore silk caps that were decorated with gold and silver, and a feather that indicated the official's Rank. The Ranks in the twelve level cap and Rank system consisted of the greater and the lesser of each of the six [[:en:Confucianism|Confucian]] virtues: {{nihongo|virtue|徳|toku}}, {{nihongo|benevolence|仁|jin}}, {{nihongo|propriety|禮|rei}}, {{nihongo|sincerity|信|shin}}, {{nihongo|justice|義|gi}} and {{nihongo|knowledge|智|chi}}.
The twelve cap system was replaced in 647.<ref name=samurai/>
==Innovations== The primary distinction between this new system and the old ''[[kabane]]'' system by which a person's Rank was determined based on heredity, was that the cap and Rank system allowed for promotion based on merit and individual achievement. One of the more well known examples of promotion within the cap and Rank system is that of [[:en:Ono no Imoko|Ono no Imoko]]. When Imoko was first sent as an envoy to the [[:en:Sui dynasty|Sui]] court in 607, he was Ranked Greater Propriety (5th Rank), but he was eventually promoted to the top Rank of Greater Virtue because of his achievements, particularly during his second trip to Sui in 608.

<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[ar:المراتب الاثنتا عشر]][[be:Сістэма дванаццаці рангаў]][[en:Twelve Level Cap and Rank System]][[fa:دوازده سطح کلاه و سیستم رتبه]][[fr:Système des douze niveaux de rang]][[ja:冠位十二階]][[ko:관위십이계]][[nl:Twaalf Hofrangen (Japan)]][[pl:System dwunastu rang]][[ru:Система двенадцати рангов]][[sh:Sistem dvanaest rangova]][[th:ระบบยศผ้าโพกหัวสิบสองชั้น]][[uk:Система дванадцяти рангів]][[zh:冠位十二阶]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[Category:Has wikidata]][[d:Q2448809]] Wikidata name: Twelve Level Cap and Rank System [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 05:32, 12 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|Wikidata entry Wikidata name: [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 10:11, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Short description|Cap and Rank systems established during the Asuka period}} {{nihongo|'''The Twelve Level Cap and Rank System'''|冠位十二階|Kan'i Jūnikai}}, established in 603, was the first of what would be several similar cap and Rank systems established during the [[:en:Asuka period|Asuka period]] of [[:en:Japanese history|Japanese history]].<ref name=samurai>{{cite web |url=http://wiki.samurai-archives.com/index.php?title=Court_Ranks |title=Court Ranks }}</ref> It was adapted from [[Nine-Rank system|similar systems]] that were already in place in [[:en:Sui dynasty|Sui dynasty]] [[:en:China|China]], [[:en:Baekje|Paekche]] and [[:en:Goguryeo|Koguryŏ]]. The officials wore silk caps that were decorated with gold and silver, and a feather that indicated the official's Rank. The Ranks in the twelve level cap and Rank system consisted of the greater and the lesser of each of the six [[:en:Confucianism|Confucian]] virtues: {{nihongo|virtue|徳|toku}}, {{nihongo|benevolence|仁|jin}}, {{nihongo|propriety|禮|rei}}, {{nihongo|sincerity|信|shin}}, {{nihongo|justice|義|gi}} and {{nihongo|knowledge|智|chi}}.
The twelve cap system was replaced in 647.<ref name=samurai/>
==Innovations== The primary distinction between this new system and the old ''[[kabane]]'' system by which a person's Rank was determined based on heredity, was that the cap and Rank system allowed for promotion based on merit and individual achievement. One of the more well known examples of promotion within the cap and Rank system is that of [[:en:Ono no Imoko|Ono no Imoko]]. When Imoko was first sent as an envoy to the [[:en:Sui dynasty|Sui]] court in 607, he was Ranked Greater Propriety (5th Rank), but he was eventually promoted to the top Rank of Greater Virtue because of his achievements, particularly during his second trip to Sui in 608.

<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[ar:المراتب الاثنتا عشر]][[be:Сістэма дванаццаці рангаў]][[en:Twelve Level Cap and Rank System]][[fa:دوازده سطح کلاه و سیستم رتبه]][[fr:Système des douze niveaux de rang]][[ja:冠位十二階]][[ko:관위십이계]][[nl:Twaalf Hofrangen (Japan)]][[pl:System dwunastu rang]][[ru:Система двенадцати рангов]][[sh:Sistem dvanaest rangova]][[th:ระบบยศผ้าโพกหัวสิบสองชั้น]][[uk:Система дванадцяти рангів]][[zh:冠位十二阶]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[Category:Has wikidata]][[d:Q2448809]] Wikidata name: Twelve Level Cap and Rank System [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 05:32, 12 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|Wikidata entry Wikidata name: [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 10:11, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Short description|Cap and Rank systems established during the Asuka period}} {{nihongo|'''The Twelve Level Cap and Rank System'''|冠位十二階|Kan'i Jūnikai}}, established in 603, was the first of what would be several similar cap and Rank systems established during the [[:en:Asuka period|Asuka period]] of [[:en:Japanese history|Japanese history]].<ref name=samurai>{{cite web |url=http://wiki.samurai-archives.com/index.php?title=Court_Ranks |title=Court Ranks }}</ref> It was adapted from [[Nine-Rank system|similar systems]] that were already in place in [[:en:Sui dynasty|Sui dynasty]] [[:en:China|China]], [[:en:Baekje|Paekche]] and [[:en:Goguryeo|Koguryŏ]]. The officials wore silk caps that were decorated with gold and silver, and a feather that indicated the official's Rank. The Ranks in the twelve level cap and Rank system consisted of the greater and the lesser of each of the six [[:en:Confucianism|Confucian]] virtues: {{nihongo|virtue|徳|toku}}, {{nihongo|benevolence|仁|jin}}, {{nihongo|propriety|禮|rei}}, {{nihongo|sincerity|信|shin}}, {{nihongo|justice|義|gi}} and {{nihongo|knowledge|智|chi}}.
The twelve cap system was replaced in 647.<ref name=samurai/>
==Innovations== The primary distinction between this new system and the old ''[[kabane]]'' system by which a person's Rank was determined based on heredity, was that the cap and Rank system allowed for promotion based on merit and individual achievement. One of the more well known examples of promotion within the cap and Rank system is that of [[:en:Ono no Imoko|Ono no Imoko]]. When Imoko was first sent as an envoy to the [[:en:Sui dynasty|Sui]] court in 607, he was Ranked Greater Propriety (5th Rank), but he was eventually promoted to the top Rank of Greater Virtue because of his achievements, particularly during his second trip to Sui in 608.
==Ranks and colors== The following table lists the various Ranks and the colors that were believed to have been assigned to each one.<ref>Yoshimura, Takehiko: 'Kodai Ōken no Tenkai (古代王権の展開)', p. 126. Shūeisha, 1999.</ref>

The officials wore silk caps that were decorated with gold and silver, and a feather that indicated the official's Rank. The Ranks in the twelve level cap and Rank system consisted of the greater and the lesser of each of the six [[:en:Confucianism|Confucian]] virtues: {{nihongo|virtue|徳|toku}}, {{nihongo|benevolence|仁|jin}}, {{nihongo|propriety|禮|rei}}, {{nihongo|sincerity|信|shin}}, {{nihongo|justice|義|gi}} and {{nihongo|knowledge|智|chi}}.
The twelve cap system was replaced in 647.<ref name=samurai/>
==Innovations== The primary distinction between this new system and the old ''[[kabane]]'' system by which a person's Rank was determined based on heredity, was that the cap and Rank system allowed for promotion based on merit and individual achievement. One of the more well known examples of promotion within the cap and Rank system is that of [[:en:Ono no Imoko|Ono no Imoko]]. When Imoko was first sent as an envoy to the [[:en:Sui dynasty|Sui]] court in 607, he was Ranked Greater Propriety (5th Rank), but he was eventually promoted to the top Rank of Greater Virtue because of his achievements, particularly during his second trip to Sui in 608.

The officials wore silk caps that were decorated with gold and silver, and a feather that indicated the official's Rank. The Ranks in the twelve level cap and Rank system consisted of the greater and the lesser of each of the six [[:en:Confucianism|Confucian]] virtues: {{nihongo|virtue|徳|toku}}, {{nihongo|benevolence|仁|jin}}, {{nihongo|propriety|禮|rei}}, {{nihongo|sincerity|信|shin}}, {{nihongo|justice|義|gi}} and {{nihongo|knowledge|智|chi}}.
The twelve cap system was replaced in 647.<ref name=samurai/>
==Innovations== The primary distinction between this new system and the old ''[[kabane]]'' system by which a person's Rank was determined based on heredity, was that the cap and Rank system allowed for promotion based on merit and individual achievement. One of the more well known examples of promotion within the cap and Rank system is that of [[:en:Ono no Imoko|Ono no Imoko]]. When Imoko was first sent as an envoy to the [[:en:Sui dynasty|Sui]] court in 607, he was Ranked Greater Propriety (5th Rank), but he was eventually promoted to the top Rank of Greater Virtue because of his achievements, particularly during his second trip to Sui in 608.

([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 10:11, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Short description|Cap and Rank systems established during the Asuka period}} {{nihongo|'''The Twelve Level Cap and Rank System'''|冠位十二階|Kan'i Jūnikai}}, established in 603, was the first of what would be several similar cap and Rank systems established during the [[:en:Asuka period|Asuka period]] of [[:en:Japanese history|Japanese history]].<ref name=samurai>{{cite web |url=http://wiki.samurai-archives.com/index.php?title=Court_Ranks |title=Court Ranks }}</ref> It was adapted from [[Nine-Rank system|similar systems]] that were already in place in [[:en:Sui dynasty|Sui dynasty]] [[:en:China|China]], [[:en:Baekje|Paekche]] and [[:en:Goguryeo|Koguryŏ]]. The officials wore silk caps that were decorated with gold and silver, and a feather that indicated the official's Rank. The Ranks in the twelve level cap and Rank system consisted of the greater and the lesser of each of the six [[:en:Confucianism|Confucian]] virtues: {{nihongo|virtue|徳|toku}}, {{nihongo|benevolence|仁|jin}}, {{nihongo|propriety|禮|rei}}, {{nihongo|sincerity|信|shin}}, {{nihongo|justice|義|gi}} and {{nihongo|knowledge|智|chi}}.
The twelve cap system was replaced in 647.<ref name=samurai/>
==Innovations== The primary distinction between this new system and the old ''[[kabane]]'' system by which a person's Rank was determined based on heredity, was that the cap and Rank system allowed for promotion based on merit and individual achievement. One of the more well known examples of promotion within the cap and Rank system is that of [[:en:Ono no Imoko|Ono no Imoko]]. When Imoko was first sent as an envoy to the [[:en:Sui dynasty|Sui]] court in 607, he was Ranked Greater Propriety (5th Rank), but he was eventually promoted to the top Rank of Greater Virtue because of his achievements, particularly during his second trip to Sui in 608.

talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 10:11, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Short description|Cap and Rank systems established during the Asuka period}} {{nihongo|'''The Twelve Level Cap and Rank System'''|冠位十二階|Kan'i Jūnikai}}, established in 603, was the first of what would be several similar cap and Rank systems established during the [[:en:Asuka period|Asuka period]] of [[:en:Japanese history|Japanese history]].<ref name=samurai>{{cite web |url=http://wiki.samurai-archives.com/index.php?title=Court_Ranks |title=Court Ranks }}</ref> It was adapted from [[Nine-Rank system|similar systems]] that were already in place in [[:en:Sui dynasty|Sui dynasty]] [[:en:China|China]], [[:en:Baekje|Paekche]] and [[:en:Goguryeo|Koguryŏ]]. The officials wore silk caps that were decorated with gold and silver, and a feather that indicated the official's Rank. The Ranks in the twelve level cap and Rank system consisted of the greater and the lesser of each of the six [[:en:Confucianism|Confucian]] virtues: {{nihongo|virtue|徳|toku}}, {{nihongo|benevolence|仁|jin}}, {{nihongo|propriety|禮|rei}}, {{nihongo|sincerity|信|shin}}, {{nihongo|justice|義|gi}} and {{nihongo|knowledge|智|chi}}.
The twelve cap system was replaced in 647.<ref name=samurai/>
==Innovations== The primary distinction between this new system and the old ''[[kabane]]'' system by which a person's Rank was determined based on heredity, was that the cap and Rank system allowed for promotion based on merit and individual achievement. One of the more well known examples of promotion within the cap and Rank system is that of [[:en:Ono no Imoko|Ono no Imoko]]. When Imoko was first sent as an envoy to the [[:en:Sui dynasty|Sui]] court in 607, he was Ranked Greater Propriety (5th Rank), but he was eventually promoted to the top Rank of Greater Virtue because of his achievements, particularly during his second trip to Sui in 608.

Jūnikai}}, established in 603, was the first of what would be several similar cap and Rank systems established during the [[:en:Asuka period|Asuka period]] of [[:en:Japanese history|Japanese history]].<ref name=samurai>{{cite web |url=http://wiki.samurai-archives.com/index.php?title=Court_Ranks |title=Court Ranks }}</ref> It was adapted from [[Nine-Rank system|similar systems]] that were already in place in [[:en:Sui dynasty|Sui dynasty]] [[:en:China|China]], [[:en:Baekje|Paekche]] and [[:en:Goguryeo|Koguryŏ]]. The officials wore silk caps that were decorated with gold and silver, and a feather that indicated the official's Rank. The Ranks in the twelve level cap and Rank system consisted of the greater and the lesser of each of the six [[:en:Confucianism|Confucian]] virtues: {{nihongo|virtue|徳|toku}}, {{nihongo|benevolence|仁|jin}}, {{nihongo|propriety|禮|rei}}, {{nihongo|sincerity|信|shin}}, {{nihongo|justice|義|gi}} and {{nihongo|knowledge|智|chi}}.
The twelve cap system was replaced in 647.<ref name=samurai/>
==Innovations== The primary distinction between this new system and the old ''[[kabane]]'' system by which a person's Rank was determined based on heredity, was that the cap and Rank system allowed for promotion based on merit and individual achievement. One of the more well known examples of promotion within the cap and Rank system is that of [[:en:Ono no Imoko|Ono no Imoko]]. When Imoko was first sent as an envoy to the [[:en:Sui dynasty|Sui]] court in 607, he was Ranked Greater Propriety (5th Rank), but he was eventually promoted to the top Rank of Greater Virtue because of his achievements, particularly during his second trip to Sui in 608.

talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 10:11, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Short description|Cap and Rank systems established during the Asuka period}} {{nihongo|'''The Twelve Level Cap and Rank System'''|冠位十二階|Kan'i Jūnikai}}, established in 603, was the first of what would be several similar cap and Rank systems established during the [[:en:Asuka period|Asuka period]] of [[:en:Japanese history|Japanese history]].<ref name=samurai>{{cite web |url=http://wiki.samurai-archives.com/index.php?title=Court_Ranks |title=Court Ranks }}</ref> It was adapted from [[Nine-Rank system|similar systems]] that were already in place in [[:en:Sui dynasty|Sui dynasty]] [[:en:China|China]], [[:en:Baekje|Paekche]] and [[:en:Goguryeo|Koguryŏ]]. The officials wore silk caps that were decorated with gold and silver, and a feather that indicated the official's Rank. The Ranks in the twelve level cap and Rank system consisted of the greater and the lesser of each of the six [[:en:Confucianism|Confucian]] virtues: {{nihongo|virtue|徳|toku}}, {{nihongo|benevolence|仁|jin}}, {{nihongo|propriety|禮|rei}}, {{nihongo|sincerity|信|shin}}, {{nihongo|justice|義|gi}} and {{nihongo|knowledge|智|chi}}.
The twelve cap system was replaced in 647.<ref name=samurai/>
==Innovations== The primary distinction between this new system and the old ''[[kabane]]'' system by which a person's Rank was determined based on heredity, was that the cap and Rank system allowed for promotion based on merit and individual achievement. One of the more well known examples of promotion within the cap and Rank system is that of [[:en:Ono no Imoko|Ono no Imoko]]. When Imoko was first sent as an envoy to the [[:en:Sui dynasty|Sui]] court in 607, he was Ranked Greater Propriety (5th Rank), but he was eventually promoted to the top Rank of Greater Virtue because of his achievements, particularly during his second trip to Sui in 608.

talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 10:11, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Short description|Cap and Rank systems established during the Asuka period}} {{nihongo|'''The Twelve Level Cap and Rank System'''|冠位十二階|Kan'i Jūnikai}}, established in 603, was the first of what would be several similar cap and Rank systems established during the [[:en:Asuka period|Asuka period]] of [[:en:Japanese history|Japanese history]].<ref name=samurai>{{cite web |url=http://wiki.samurai-archives.com/index.php?title=Court_Ranks |title=Court Ranks }}</ref> It was adapted from [[Nine-Rank system|similar systems]] that were already in place in [[:en:Sui dynasty|Sui dynasty]] [[:en:China|China]], [[:en:Baekje|Paekche]] and [[:en:Goguryeo|Koguryŏ]]. The officials wore silk caps that were decorated with gold and silver, and a feather that indicated the official's Rank. The Ranks in the twelve level cap and Rank system consisted of the greater and the lesser of each of the six [[:en:Confucianism|Confucian]] virtues: {{nihongo|virtue|徳|toku}}, {{nihongo|benevolence|仁|jin}}, {{nihongo|propriety|禮|rei}}, {{nihongo|sincerity|信|shin}}, {{nihongo|justice|義|gi}} and {{nihongo|knowledge|智|chi}}.
The twelve cap system was replaced in 647.<ref name=samurai/>
==Innovations== The primary distinction between this new system and the old ''[[kabane]]'' system by which a person's Rank was determined based on heredity, was that the cap and Rank system allowed for promotion based on merit and individual achievement. One of the more well known examples of promotion within the cap and Rank system is that of [[:en:Ono no Imoko|Ono no Imoko]]. When Imoko was first sent as an envoy to the [[:en:Sui dynasty|Sui]] court in 607, he was Ranked Greater Propriety (5th Rank), but he was eventually promoted to the top Rank of Greater Virtue because of his achievements, particularly during his second trip to Sui in 608.
==Ranks and colors== The following table lists the various Ranks and the colors that were believed to have been assigned to each one.<ref>Yoshimura, Takehiko: 'Kodai Ōken no Tenkai (古代王権の展開)', p. 126. Shūeisha, 1999.</ref>

Jūnikai}}, established in 603, was the first of what would be several similar cap and Rank systems established during the [[:en:Asuka period|Asuka period]] of [[:en:Japanese history|Japanese history]].<ref name=samurai>{{cite web |url=http://wiki.samurai-archives.com/index.php?title=Court_Ranks |title=Court Ranks }}</ref> It was adapted from [[Nine-Rank system|similar systems]] that were already in place in [[:en:Sui dynasty|Sui dynasty]] [[:en:China|China]], [[:en:Baekje|Paekche]] and [[:en:Goguryeo|Koguryŏ]]. The officials wore silk caps that were decorated with gold and silver, and a feather that indicated the official's Rank. The Ranks in the twelve level cap and Rank system consisted of the greater and the lesser of each of the six [[:en:Confucianism|Confucian]] virtues: {{nihongo|virtue|徳|toku}}, {{nihongo|benevolence|仁|jin}}, {{nihongo|propriety|禮|rei}}, {{nihongo|sincerity|信|shin}}, {{nihongo|justice|義|gi}} and {{nihongo|knowledge|智|chi}}.
The twelve cap system was replaced in 647.<ref name=samurai/>
==Innovations== The primary distinction between this new system and the old ''[[kabane]]'' system by which a person's Rank was determined based on heredity, was that the cap and Rank system allowed for promotion based on merit and individual achievement. One of the more well known examples of promotion within the cap and Rank system is that of [[:en:Ono no Imoko|Ono no Imoko]]. When Imoko was first sent as an envoy to the [[:en:Sui dynasty|Sui]] court in 607, he was Ranked Greater Propriety (5th Rank), but he was eventually promoted to the top Rank of Greater Virtue because of his achievements, particularly during his second trip to Sui in 608.

talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 10:11, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Short description|Cap and Rank systems established during the Asuka period}} {{nihongo|'''The Twelve Level Cap and Rank System'''|冠位十二階|Kan'i Jūnikai}}, established in 603, was the first of what would be several similar cap and Rank systems established during the [[:en:Asuka period|Asuka period]] of [[:en:Japanese history|Japanese history]].<ref name=samurai>{{cite web |url=http://wiki.samurai-archives.com/index.php?title=Court_Ranks |title=Court Ranks }}</ref> It was adapted from [[Nine-Rank system|similar systems]] that were already in place in [[:en:Sui dynasty|Sui dynasty]] [[:en:China|China]], [[:en:Baekje|Paekche]] and [[:en:Goguryeo|Koguryŏ]]. The officials wore silk caps that were decorated with gold and silver, and a feather that indicated the official's Rank. The Ranks in the twelve level cap and Rank system consisted of the greater and the lesser of each of the six [[:en:Confucianism|Confucian]] virtues: {{nihongo|virtue|徳|toku}}, {{nihongo|benevolence|仁|jin}}, {{nihongo|propriety|禮|rei}}, {{nihongo|sincerity|信|shin}}, {{nihongo|justice|義|gi}} and {{nihongo|knowledge|智|chi}}.
The twelve cap system was replaced in 647.<ref name=samurai/>
==Innovations== The primary distinction between this new system and the old ''[[kabane]]'' system by which a person's Rank was determined based on heredity, was that the cap and Rank system allowed for promotion based on merit and individual achievement. One of the more well known examples of promotion within the cap and Rank system is that of [[:en:Ono no Imoko|Ono no Imoko]]. When Imoko was first sent as an envoy to the [[:en:Sui dynasty|Sui]] court in 607, he was Ranked Greater Propriety (5th Rank), but he was eventually promoted to the top Rank of Greater Virtue because of his achievements, particularly during his second trip to Sui in 608.

talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 10:11, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Short description|Cap and Rank systems established during the Asuka period}} {{nihongo|'''The Twelve Level Cap and Rank System'''|冠位十二階|Kan'i Jūnikai}}, established in 603, was the first of what would be several similar cap and Rank systems established during the {{ill|Asuka period|en|Asuka period|WD=Q210688|lt=Asuka period}} of [[:en:Japanese history|Japanese history]].<ref name=samurai>{{cite web |url=http://wiki.samurai-archives.com/index.php?title=Court_Ranks |title=Court Ranks }}</ref> It was adapted from [[Nine-Rank system|similar systems]] that were already in place in {{ill|Sui dynasty|en|Sui dynasty|WD=Q7405|lt=Sui dynasty}} {{ill|China|en|China|WD=Q148|lt=China}}, [[:en:Baekje|Paekche]] and {{ill|Goguryeo|en|Goguryeo|WD=Q28370|lt=Koguryŏ}}. The officials wore silk caps that were decorated with gold and silver, and a feather that indicated the official's Rank. The Ranks in the twelve level cap and Rank system consisted of the greater and the lesser of each of the six {{ill|Confucianism|en|Confucianism|WD=Q9581|lt=Confucian}} virtues: {{nihongo|virtue|徳|toku}}, {{nihongo|benevolence|仁|jin}}, {{nihongo|propriety|禮|rei}}, {{nihongo|sincerity|信|shin}}, {{nihongo|justice|義|gi}} and {{nihongo|knowledge|智|chi}}.
The twelve cap system was replaced in 647.<ref name=samurai/>
==Innovations== The primary distinction between this new system and the old ''[[kabane]]'' system by which a person's Rank was determined based on heredity, was that the cap and Rank system allowed for promotion based on merit and individual achievement. One of the more well known examples of promotion within the cap and Rank system is that of {{ill|Ono no Imoko|en|Ono no Imoko|WD=Q1284072|lt=Ono no Imoko}}. When Imoko was first sent as an envoy to the {{ill|Sui dynasty|en|Sui dynasty|WD=Q7405|lt=Sui}} court in 607, he was Ranked Greater Propriety (5th Rank), but he was eventually promoted to the top Rank of Greater Virtue because of his achievements, particularly during his second trip to Sui in 608.
==Ranks and colors== The following table lists the various Ranks and the colors that were believed to have been assigned to each one.<ref>Yoshimura, Takehiko: 'Kodai Ōken no Tenkai (古代王権の展開)', p. 126. Shūeisha, 1999.</ref>

talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 10:11, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Short description|Cap and Rank systems established during the Asuka period}} {{nihongo|'''The Twelve Level Cap and Rank System'''|冠位十二階|Kan'i Jūnikai}}, established in 603, was the first of what would be several similar cap and Rank systems established during the {{ill|Asuka period|en|Asuka period|WD=Q210688|lt=Asuka period}} of [[:en:Japanese history|Japanese history]].<ref name=samurai>{{cite web |url=http://wiki.samurai-archives.com/index.php?title=Court_Ranks |title=Court Ranks }}</ref> It was adapted from [[Nine-Rank system|similar systems]] that were already in place in {{ill|Sui dynasty|en|Sui dynasty|WD=Q7405|lt=Sui dynasty}} {{ill|China|en|China|WD=Q148|lt=China}}, [[:en:Baekje|Paekche]] and {{ill|Goguryeo|en|Goguryeo|WD=Q28370|lt=Koguryŏ}}. The officials wore silk caps that were decorated with gold and silver, and a feather that indicated the official's Rank. The Ranks in the twelve level cap and Rank system consisted of the greater and the lesser of each of the six {{ill|Confucianism|en|Confucianism|WD=Q9581|lt=Confucian}} virtues: {{nihongo|virtue|徳|toku}}, {{nihongo|benevolence|仁|jin}}, {{nihongo|propriety|禮|rei}}, {{nihongo|sincerity|信|shin}}, {{nihongo|justice|義|gi}} and {{nihongo|knowledge|智|chi}}.
The twelve cap system was replaced in 647.<ref name=samurai/>
==Innovations== The primary distinction between this new system and the old ''[[kabane]]'' system by which a person's Rank was determined based on heredity, was that the cap and Rank system allowed for promotion based on merit and individual achievement. One of the more well known examples of promotion within the cap and Rank system is that of {{ill|Ono no Imoko|en|Ono no Imoko|WD=Q1284072|lt=Ono no Imoko}}. When Imoko was first sent as an envoy to the {{ill|Sui dynasty|en|Sui dynasty|WD=Q7405|lt=Sui}} court in 607, he was Ranked Greater Propriety (5th Rank), but he was eventually promoted to the top Rank of Greater Virtue because of his achievements, particularly during his second trip to Sui in 608.

{{Short description|Cap and Rank systems established during the Asuka period}} {{nihongo|'''The Twelve Level Cap and Rank System'''|冠位十二階|Kan'i Jūnikai}}, established in 603, was the first of what would be several similar cap and Rank systems established during the {{ill|Asuka period|en|Asuka period|WD=Q210688|lt=Asuka period}} of [[:en:Japanese history|Japanese history]].<ref name=samurai>{{cite web |url=http://wiki.samurai-archives.com/index.php?title=Court_Ranks |title=Court Ranks }}</ref> It was adapted from [[Nine-Rank system|similar systems]] that were already in place in {{ill|Sui dynasty|en|Sui dynasty|WD=Q7405|lt=Sui dynasty}} {{ill|China|en|China|WD=Q148|lt=China}}, [[:en:Baekje|Paekche]] and {{ill|Goguryeo|en|Goguryeo|WD=Q28370|lt=Koguryŏ}}. The officials wore silk caps that were decorated with gold and silver, and a feather that indicated the official's Rank. The Ranks in the twelve level cap and Rank system consisted of the greater and the lesser of each of the six {{ill|Confucianism|en|Confucianism|WD=Q9581|lt=Confucian}} virtues: {{nihongo|virtue|徳|toku}}, {{nihongo|benevolence|仁|jin}}, {{nihongo|propriety|禮|rei}}, {{nihongo|sincerity|信|shin}}, {{nihongo|justice|義|gi}} and {{nihongo|knowledge|智|chi}}.
The twelve cap system was replaced in 647.<ref name=samurai/>
==Innovations== The primary distinction between this new system and the old ''[[kabane]]'' system by which a person's Rank was determined based on heredity, was that the cap and Rank system allowed for promotion based on merit and individual achievement. One of the more well known examples of promotion within the cap and Rank system is that of {{ill|Ono no Imoko|en|Ono no Imoko|WD=Q1284072|lt=Ono no Imoko}}. When Imoko was first sent as an envoy to the {{ill|Sui dynasty|en|Sui dynasty|WD=Q7405|lt=Sui}} court in 607, he was Ranked Greater Propriety (5th Rank), but he was eventually promoted to the top Rank of Greater Virtue because of his achievements, particularly during his second trip to Sui in 608.
==Ranks and colors== The following table lists the various Ranks and the colors that were believed to have been assigned to each one.<ref>Yoshimura, Takehiko: 'Kodai Ōken no Tenkai (古代王権の展開)', p. 126. Shūeisha, 1999.</ref>

{{Short description|Cap and Rank systems established during the Asuka period}} {{nihongo|'''The Twelve Level Cap and Rank System'''|冠位十二階|Kan'i Jūnikai}}, established in 603, was the first of what would be several similar cap and Rank systems established during the {{ill|Asuka period|en|Asuka period|WD=Q210688|lt=Asuka period}} of [[:en:Japanese history|Japanese history]].<ref name=samurai>{{cite web |url=http://wiki.samurai-archives.com/index.php?title=Court_Ranks |title=Court Ranks }}</ref> It was adapted from [[Nine-Rank system|similar systems]] that were already in place in {{ill|Sui dynasty|en|Sui dynasty|WD=Q7405|lt=Sui dynasty}} {{ill|China|en|China|WD=Q148|lt=China}}, [[:en:Baekje|Paekche]] and {{ill|Goguryeo|en|Goguryeo|WD=Q28370|lt=Koguryŏ}}. The officials wore silk caps that were decorated with gold and silver, and a feather that indicated the official's Rank. The Ranks in the twelve level cap and Rank system consisted of the greater and the lesser of each of the six {{ill|Confucianism|en|Confucianism|WD=Q9581|lt=Confucian}} virtues: {{nihongo|virtue|徳|toku}}, {{nihongo|benevolence|仁|jin}}, {{nihongo|propriety|禮|rei}}, {{nihongo|sincerity|信|shin}}, {{nihongo|justice|義|gi}} and {{nihongo|knowledge|智|chi}}.
The twelve cap system was replaced in 647.<ref name=samurai/>
==Innovations== The primary distinction between this new system and the old ''[[kabane]]'' system by which a person's Rank was determined based on heredity, was that the cap and Rank system allowed for promotion based on merit and individual achievement. One of the more well known examples of promotion within the cap and Rank system is that of {{ill|Ono no Imoko|en|Ono no Imoko|WD=Q1284072|lt=Ono no Imoko}}. When Imoko was first sent as an envoy to the {{ill|Sui dynasty|en|Sui dynasty|WD=Q7405|lt=Sui}} court in 607, he was Ranked Greater Propriety (5th Rank), but he was eventually promoted to the top Rank of Greater Virtue because of his achievements, particularly during his second trip to Sui in 608.

{{Short description|Cap and Rank systems established during the Asuka period}} {{nihongo|'''The Twelve Level Cap and Rank System'''|冠位十二階|Kan'i Jūnikai}}, established in 603, was the first of what would be several similar cap and Rank systems established during the {{ill|Asuka period|en|Asuka period|WD=Q210688|lt=Asuka period|1=Asuka period}} of [[:en:Japanese history|Japanese history]].<ref name=samurai>{{cite web |url=http://wiki.samurai-archives.com/index.php?title=Court_Ranks |title=Court Ranks }}</ref> It was adapted from [[Nine-Rank system|similar systems]] that were already in place in {{ill|Sui dynasty|en|Sui dynasty|WD=Q7405|lt=Sui dynasty|1=Sui dynasty}} {{ill|China|en|China|WD=Q148|lt=China|1=China}}, [[:en:Baekje|Paekche]] and {{ill|Goguryeo|en|Goguryeo|WD=Q28370|lt=Koguryŏ|1=Goguryeo}}. The officials wore silk caps that were decorated with gold and silver, and a feather that indicated the official's Rank. The Ranks in the twelve level cap and Rank system consisted of the greater and the lesser of each of the six {{ill|Confucianism|en|Confucianism|WD=Q9581|lt=Confucian|1=Confucianism}} virtues: {{nihongo|virtue|徳|toku}}, {{nihongo|benevolence|仁|jin}}, {{nihongo|propriety|禮|rei}}, {{nihongo|sincerity|信|shin}}, {{nihongo|justice|義|gi}} and {{nihongo|knowledge|智|chi}}.
The twelve cap system was replaced in 647.<ref name=samurai/>
==Innovations== The primary distinction between this new system and the old ''[[kabane]]'' system by which a person's Rank was determined based on heredity, was that the cap and Rank system allowed for promotion based on merit and individual achievement. One of the more well known examples of promotion within the cap and Rank system is that of {{ill|Ono no Imoko|en|Ono no Imoko|WD=Q1284072|lt=Ono no Imoko|1=Ono no Imoko}}. When Imoko was first sent as an envoy to the {{ill|Sui dynasty|en|Sui dynasty|WD=Q7405|lt=Sui|1=Sui dynasty}} court in 607, he was Ranked Greater Propriety (5th Rank), but he was eventually promoted to the top Rank of Greater Virtue because of his achievements, particularly during his second trip to Sui in 608.
==Ranks and colors== The following table lists the various Ranks and the colors that were believed to have been assigned to each one.<ref>Yoshimura, Takehiko: 'Kodai Ōken no Tenkai (古代王権の展開)', p. 126. Shūeisha, 1999.</ref>

{{Short description|Cap and Rank systems established during the Asuka period}} {{nihongo|'''The Twelve Level Cap and Rank System'''|冠位十二階|Kan'i Jūnikai}}, established in 603, was the first of what would be several similar cap and Rank systems established during the {{ill|Asuka period|en|Asuka period|WD=Q210688|lt=Asuka period|1=Asuka period}} of [[:en:Japanese history|Japanese history]].<ref name=samurai>{{cite web |url=http://wiki.samurai-archives.com/index.php?title=Court_Ranks |title=Court Ranks }}</ref> It was adapted from [[Nine-Rank system|similar systems]] that were already in place in {{ill|Sui dynasty|en|Sui dynasty|WD=Q7405|lt=Sui dynasty|1=Sui dynasty}} {{ill|China|en|China|WD=Q148|lt=China|1=China}}, [[:en:Baekje|Paekche]] and {{ill|Goguryeo|en|Goguryeo|WD=Q28370|lt=Koguryŏ|1=Goguryeo}}. The officials wore silk caps that were decorated with gold and silver, and a feather that indicated the official's Rank. The Ranks in the twelve level cap and Rank system consisted of the greater and the lesser of each of the six {{ill|Confucianism|en|Confucianism|WD=Q9581|lt=Confucian|1=Confucianism}} virtues: {{nihongo|virtue|徳|toku}}, {{nihongo|benevolence|仁|jin}}, {{nihongo|propriety|禮|rei}}, {{nihongo|sincerity|信|shin}}, {{nihongo|justice|義|gi}} and {{nihongo|knowledge|智|chi}}.
The twelve cap system was replaced in 647.<ref name=samurai/>
==Innovations== The primary distinction between this new system and the old ''[[kabane]]'' system by which a person's Rank was determined based on heredity, was that the cap and Rank system allowed for promotion based on merit and individual achievement. One of the more well known examples of promotion within the cap and Rank system is that of {{ill|Ono no Imoko|en|Ono no Imoko|WD=Q1284072|lt=Ono no Imoko|1=Ono no Imoko}}. When Imoko was first sent as an envoy to the {{ill|Sui dynasty|en|Sui dynasty|WD=Q7405|lt=Sui|1=Sui dynasty}} court in 607, he was Ranked Greater Propriety (5th Rank), but he was eventually promoted to the top Rank of Greater Virtue because of his achievements, particularly during his second trip to Sui in 608.
